name: Straight sinus and inferior sagittal sinus
summary: The inferior sagittal sinus runs in the free edge of the falx above the corpus callosum and joins the great cerebral vein of Galen at the anterior edge of the tentorium to form the straight sinus, which runs backward along the junction of the falx and tentorium to the confluence. The straight sinus therefore drains the deep venous system (internal cerebral and basal veins) from the thalami, basal ganglia and deep white matter; its thrombosis produces bilateral thalamic edema, coma and a picture easily confused with an artery of Percheron infarct or a tumor.

anatomy.location: Inferior sagittal sinus in the lower free margin of the falx; straight sinus from the falcotentorial junction behind the splenium to the internal occipital protuberance, sloping downward and backward.

function: Drainage of the deep cerebral veins (via the vein of Galen) and the medial hemisphere (inferior sagittal sinus) to the confluence of sinuses.

arteries: (venous structure) drains territories of the cerebral arteries

bestView.label: straight sinus along the falcotentorial junction behind the splenium
straight sinus running back to the confluence

imaging.normalAppearance: A straight dark channel from the splenium to the occipital protuberance on sagittal T1/T2 and venography; thrombosis shows as absent flow with T1-bright clot and bilateral thalamic swelling.

pathology.pathology: Deep venous thrombosis (straight sinus, vein of Galen, internal cerebral veins)
pathology.finding: Absent flow in the deep venous system with bilateral thalamic and basal ganglia edema and hemorrhage.
pathology.pitfalls: Bilateral thalamic swelling without diffusion restriction: check the venogram before diagnosing tumor or Percheron infarct

pathology.finding: Enhancing mass at the falcotentorial junction compressing the straight sinus.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: MR venography with T1 and SWI

lesionEffects.deficit: Coma or fluctuating consciousness with bilateral thalamic swelling
Memory and behavioral change after recovery

examination: Level of consciousness and vertical gaze
pearls: Bilateral thalamic edema in a young person: deep venous thrombosis first, then everything else
The straight sinus is the exit for the whole deep venous system: its occlusion is more dangerous than a lateral sinus occlusion
